home.title: One academic platform your institution runs itself
home.subtitle: The institution enters its own data once. Everything after that is one record: the timetable, the coursework, the exam period and the grade, read through whatever permissions a person holds.

problem.title: The registry is one system, the teaching is another
problem.body: A university keeps its programmes, enrolments and grades in one system and runs its teaching in a second. The seam between them is where a deadline goes missing, where a grade is a calculation here and a record there, and where the work of putting the two together lands on the student. StudViro is one system that does both jobs.

one.title: Nothing arrives by import
one.body: The institution enters a term, an offering or a cohort itself, and that entry is the record. There is no nightly job and nothing to reconcile afterwards.

two.title: Nothing is lost track of
two.body: Every grade published, role granted and enrolment corrected lands in an audit trail with a name and a time on it.

three.title: Nothing is over-shared
three.body: What a person sees is decided by a scoped permission, on the server.

features.title: What it does today
features.subtitle: Shipped and in use, not roadmap.

dashboard.title: A dashboard that answers "what now?"
dashboard.body: This term's courses, the latest results and the rest of your week on one screen, each item linking through to the thing behind it.

calendar.title: One week, three layers
calendar.body: Classes, exam terms and assignment deadlines in a single week view, filterable by course and by type, for the courses you attend and the ones you teach.

course.title: A course page with everything on it
course.body: Materials, assignments, staff, study groups, the timetable, the exam terms and your own marks, instead of four tabs across two systems.

grades.title: Calculated, proposed, official
grades.body: The three are shown as what they are rather than blended into one number. A resit sits beside the attempt it follows, an annulled result says so, and a programme standing counts credits earned against credits left.

exams.title: Exam terms you can act on
exams.body: Seats, registration window and examiner, filterable by whether you may register. When you may not, the server says why rather than greying out a button.

registry.title: The year, entered once
registry.body: Terms, programmes, courses, offerings, rooms, timetables and exam periods, each behind the permission that owns it. A term's course list or a whole cohort can be pasted in from a spreadsheet.

audiences.title: Built for the three people who use it
audiences.subtitle: The same record, read three ways.

students.title: Students
students.body: One timetable, your coursework and your marks on the record your institution keeps, and an exam registration that tells you why a seat is out of reach.

teachers.title: Teachers
teachers.body: The offerings you lead, the work handed in against each of them, and your own teaching week, without opening a second system to assemble it.

institutions.title: Institutions
institutions.body: Run the whole academic year in one place: the catalogue, enrolment, timetables, exams, coursework and grades, with every permission checked at the scope it belongs to.

connect.title: 1. Set up the institution
connect.body: An administrator creates the institution, its org units and its first administrator, then enters the programmes and courses it offers.

import.title: 2. Fill the year
import.body: Terms, offerings, timetables and exam terms go in once. A term's course list or a whole cohort can be pasted straight from a spreadsheet, with a dry run that shows what would change before anything is written.

use.title: 3. Use one surface
use.body: Students, teachers and registrars each get a dashboard, a calendar and a course page over the same record. Teachers set work and mark it there; students read the result there.

trust.title: What we do with your data
trust.subtitle: The parts a registrar asks about first.

credentials.title: Credentials are write-only
credentials.body: Passwords are argon2. Sessions rotate. Nothing sensitive is echoed back, not even to an administrator.

permissions.title: Permissions carry a scope
permissions.body: Every grant names both what it permits and where. Holding the permission to read enrolments never opens a list of someone's classmates.

audit.title: Every change has a name on it
audit.body: Who proposed a grade, who published it, who granted or revoked a role, and when. The trail is readable by an institution administrator and by nobody else.

privacy.title: Data a person can take with them
privacy.body: Anybody can export what the institution holds about them. An erasure anonymises the person and keeps the academic record, so a degree does not disappear along with a name.

accessibility.title: Usable without a mouse
accessibility.body: WCAG 2.2 AA, checked in the test suite rather than claimed: real headings, a skip link, visible focus and contrast that survives both themes.

hosting.title: Your infrastructure, if you want it
hosting.body: The API is a Docker image against PostgreSQL and Redis. An institution that needs the student record inside its own network can hold it there.

replace.question: Does this replace AIS2 and Moodle?
replace.answer: That is the point. StudViro is the system of record: the institution enters its own data and there is no upstream. Both halves are built. The registry covers programmes, offerings, enrolment, timetables, exams and grades; the teaching side covers course pages, materials, assignments, hand-in and marking.

migration.question: We have years of data in a system that already runs. What happens to it?
migration.answer: Honestly: there is no importer. StudViro reads nothing from anywhere, by design. A one-off import can be written against a real export when somebody needs one, and in the meantime a term goes in by hand or by paste. Ask us about this early rather than late.

missing.question: What is not in it?
missing.answer: Signing in with a university account, because it needs a client registration only your IT can make. Recording an absence. Importing from a system you already run. Quizzes are not missing but ruled out: StudViro takes work in and marks it by hand, and nothing is planned that asks questions.

accounts.question: How do people get accounts?
accounts.answer: An institution onboards with us. Accounts are invited rather than opened from the public internet, and university single sign-on is on the roadmap.

cost.question: What does it cost?
cost.answer: We do not publish a price. Terms depend on your size and how much of the year you want to run here, so a conversation is the honest answer.

closing.title: See it with a term of your own
closing.body: Bring one department and one term. We will run the demo against a shape you recognise, and be explicit about what is not there yet.

footer.tagline: One academic platform an institution runs itself.

meta.title: For students
meta.description: One timetable, your coursework and your marks in one place, and exam registration that explains itself.

hero.title: Stop assembling your own timetable
hero.subtitle: Your courses, your week, the work you owe and your results in one place, on the record your university keeps.

week.title: Your whole week in one view
week.body: Classes, exam terms and assignment deadlines as three layers of the same week, filterable by course and by type.

courses.title: Your courses, by term
courses.body: Every enrolment with its status, and a course page carrying the staff, the materials, your study groups, the work set and your own marks.

coursework.title: Hand it in here
coursework.body: Upload against an assignment with a note to whoever marks it, resubmit up to the attempt limit the teacher set, and let the server decide what counts as late instead of arguing about it.

grades.title: A grade that says which grade it is
grades.body: Calculated, proposed and official are shown as what they are rather than blended into one number. An annulled result says so, a resit sits beside the attempt it follows, and your programme standing counts credits earned against credits left.

exams.title: Registration that gives you a reason
exams.body: Register and cancel from any exam term. When you cannot, the server answers why instead of greying out a button.

notifications.title: Told once, not five times
notifications.body: An exam term published, moved or cancelled, a grade published or corrected, an enrolment confirmed or refused: you hear about each once, deduplicated to one message per thing per day.

roadmap.title: Not yet
roadmap.body: Signing in with your university account is not built; for now the institution invites you and you claim the account. Quizzes are not coming at all: StudViro takes work in and marks it by hand.

closing.title: Ask your university about it
closing.body: StudViro is deployed by an institution, not signed up for individually. If your university is evaluating it, this is the page to send them.

meta.title: For teachers
meta.description: The offerings you lead, the work handed in against them, and your teaching week, in one place.

hero.title: Your teaching, without the second login
hero.subtitle: The offerings you lead, the students in each of them, the work they hand in and your own week, over the same record your students read.

offerings.title: Everything you lead, by term
offerings.body: Your teaching assignments with your role on each and how many students are actually enrolled.

roster.title: A roster that agrees with itself
roster.body: The student list and the enrolment count exclude withdrawn and rejected enrolments, and always match.

page.title: Build the course page yourself
page.body: Open a space against the offering, keep it unpublished while you fill it, then add files, links and text in the order you want them read. A hidden material stays invisible until you say otherwise.

assignments.title: Set work and take it in
assignments.body: A brief, an open date, a due date, a close date and an attempt policy. The server decides what counts as late, and every assignment opens its own gradebook column.

grades.title: Mark it, then publish it
grades.body: Score against the maximum with written feedback, propose a grade from the course page, and publish it separately if you hold that. A resit is a second attempt beside the first rather than an overwrite.

calendar.title: One week, teaching included
calendar.body: The calendar scopes to the offerings you teach as well as the ones you attend.

roadmap.title: Not yet
roadmap.body: An absence cannot be recorded: publishing a grade marks a seat attended, and nothing lets you mark one missed or excused. Quizzes are ruled out rather than pending.

closing.title: See it with your own courses
closing.body: A demo runs against a populated institution, so you can look at an offering you recognise.

meta.title: For institutions
meta.description: One academic platform an institution runs itself: catalogue, enrolment, timetables, exams, coursework and grades in one record.

hero.title: The whole academic year, in one system you own
hero.subtitle: The institution enters its own data, and every audience reads the same record through the permissions it holds. There is no upstream system to keep in step.

roles.title: Roles that mean something
roles.body: Eight canonical roles over a scope tree. A student role derives from an active programme membership and a teacher role from a teaching assignment, so neither is handed out by mistake.

scopes.title: Scoped role administration
scopes.body: Grant and revoke against a scope, with the hierarchy enforced on the server rather than hinted at in the interface. A person can only hand out a role they hold themselves.

catalogue.title: A catalogue you correct yourself
catalogue.body: Programmes, courses, academic terms and offerings, entered and fixed in place. A course runs at most once per term, and a term that ends before it starts is refused rather than saved.

scheduling.title: Rooms, timetable, exam period
scheduling.body: Rooms with seat counts that refuse to retire while a class still meets in them; a slot that repeats weekly to the end of term and lets a single week move or be called off; exam terms with a capacity and a registration window.

bulk.title: A term's worth at a time
bulk.body: Paste a course list or a cohort from a spreadsheet, tab, semicolon or comma separated. A dry run shows what would change before anything is written.

model.title: One canonical model
model.body: One schema for the whole academic year, from org units and rooms to results and notifications, with soft deletion and keyset pagination throughout. Every row belongs to an institution and nothing crosses between them.

containers.title: Containers you host
containers.body: A NestJS API on PostgreSQL and Redis, with migrations gated on startup so a replica never serves a schema it is behind.

contract.title: A generated API contract
contract.body: The client is generated from a drift-checked OpenAPI document, so the interface and the API cannot disagree.

demo.title: Something to open on day one
demo.body: A seed writes about seven thousand linked rows across twenty tables: a synthetic university with faculties, terms, courses, teachers, students, enrolments, timetables and results, so an evaluation starts with a populated system.

roadmap.title: What is missing, named
roadmap.subtitle: Ask about timelines rather than assuming them.

sso.title: University single sign-on
sso.body: OIDC against your identity provider. Blocked on a client registration only your IT department can make.

migration.title: Import from what you run now
migration.body: There is no importer. Today the year goes in by hand or by paste. A one-off import can be written against a real export, and that is a conversation to have before a pilot rather than after.

absence.title: Attendance
absence.body: Publishing a grade marks a seat attended. Marking one missed or excused exists in the schema and on no screen.

closing.title: Bring one department and one term
closing.body: The most useful demo runs against a scope you recognise. Tell us how your year is shaped and we will show you what the platform covers.
